columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: 300M+ tracks ad-free for Premium subscribers, plus music videos, live performances, covers, and rare tracks from the YouTube catalog.
Free tier: ad-supported on-demand songs, music videos, and podcasts; background play and downloads primarily for podcasts.
Premium: background play for music, ad-free tracks, audio-only mode, offline downloads, and Ask Music (AI mix suggestions).

strengths.title: Unique access to YouTube’s music universe
strengths.detail: Music videos, live performances, and rare uploads can live in playlists, unmatched content diversity vs pure audio catalogs.

strengths.title: Integrated short-form discovery
strengths.detail: Samples tab offers personalized short video clips to discover new songs via immersive previews.

strengths.title: Strong recommendation algorithms
strengths.detail: Personalized mixes, radio stations, and smart downloads powered by YouTube’s recommendation engine.

strengths.title: Multi-device flexibility
strengths.detail: Web, mobile, smart TVs, speakers, and Google ecosystem; upload your own library (up to 100,000 files) for ad-free playback.

weaknesses.title: Free tier limitations for music
weaknesses.detail: Background play and offline downloads for music require Premium; free tier is more limited than Spotify’s free offering.

weaknesses.title: UX complexity vs dedicated music apps
weaknesses.detail: Blend of video, audio, and discovery can feel less straightforward than pure audio apps.

weaknesses.title: Less audiophile focus
weaknesses.detail: Huge catalog, but not positioned as a Hi-Res audiophile service compared to Amazon Music HD or Qobuz.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. YouTube Music is audio streaming / listening at scale. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

With the YouTube Music app, you can watch music videos, stay connected to artists you love, and discover music and podcasts to enjoy on all your devices.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and YouTube Music side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On YouTube Music you can use Audio and Memberships as first-class product jobs. You want a dedicated listening app, playlists, and the catalog people already pay a subscription for.

Using Kahana with YouTube Music

You can use both. YouTube Music keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep listening on YouTube Music, where the catalog and players are strongest. Put episode lists, companion notes, and Club discussion on Kahana so assigned audio is a library item, not only a For You row.
